adventure.title: Puzzle Over Coral Castle
adventure.description: One man spent 28 years single-handedly carving and moving 1,100 tons of coral rock into a monument to lost love — nobody has ever fully explained how. Homestead's strangest hour.
adventure.bonus: Try to move the nine-ton gate that used to spin at a finger's touch — then read how he might have done it.

adventure.title: Canoe to Chicken Key from the Deering Estate
adventure.description: The Deering Estate's guided paddles cross a mile of open bay to Chicken Key, a seven-acre mangrove island rookery — haul out on the sand spit and swim before the return crossing.
adventure.bonus: Circle the island once before landing — herons and spoonbills nest on the far side.

adventure.title: Airboat the Glades at Coopertown
adventure.description: The original Everglades airboat outfit — running since 1945 eleven miles west of the turnpike — throttles you across the sawgrass river to gator holes the highway crowd never sees.
adventure.bonus: Eat the frog legs at the Coopertown restaurant afterward — you were warned.

adventure.title: Cable Wakeboarding at Miami Watersports Complex
adventure.description: The cable system at Amelia Earhart Park pulls you lap after lap over flat water with no boat required — beginners welcome, faceplants guaranteed, progress fast.
adventure.bonus: Attempt a board grab on your next jump — fall counts as credit for trying.

adventure.title: Parasailing over South Beach with Island Queen
adventure.description: Eight hundred feet above the Atlantic off South Beach, the whole skyline, the port, and the reef line snap into one view — book with any of the marina operators and go on a clear morning.
adventure.bonus: Go tandem with a stranger you just met on the dock.

adventure.title: Full-Moon Paddle at Virginia Key Outdoor Center
adventure.description: VKOC's guided night paddles slide you through Virginia Key's mangrove lagoons under moonlight with the downtown skyline glowing across the bay.
adventure.bonus: Submerge your hand and drag it slowly — count how many bioluminescent streaks you make in one pass.

adventure.title: Surfing at Haulover Beach
adventure.description: When a swell hits, Haulover's north end breaks cleaner than anywhere else in Miami-Dade, pulling a tight crew of locals who know the city secretly has real surf.
adventure.bonus: Paddle out to the lineup and ask a local which swell direction makes the spot work best.

adventure.title: Jet Ski Rental at Miami Beach Marina
adventure.description: Launch into Government Cut, the main shipping channel, and watch cargo ships dwarf you as you carve around the Port of Miami at 55 mph.
adventure.bonus: Ride all the way to Star Island and circle a celebrity mega-mansion.

adventure.title: Deep-Sea Fishing Charter out of Bayside
adventure.description: Miami sits on the edge of the Gulf Stream — book a half-day charter out of Bayside and you're trolling for mahi-mahi in water so blue it looks fake.
adventure.bonus: Negotiate with the captain to fillet and pack your catch — then cook it that night.

adventure.title: Snorkeling Biscayne National Park Coral Reef
adventure.description: Ninety-five percent water, Biscayne is one of the only national parks where the main attraction is an offshore living reef you can reach by ferry and drop into in minutes.
adventure.bonus: Stay under until you spot a sea turtle — don't surface until you do.

adventure.title: Dawn Paddle Through Oleta River State Park
adventure.description: Florida's largest urban park hides a mangrove tunnel maze that swallows all city noise the second you dip your paddle in.
adventure.bonus: Find the hidden sandbar inside the mangrove network and eat breakfast there.

adventure.title: Kiteboarding at Hobie Beach
adventure.description: The steady Biscayne Bay wind turns this narrow strip between the MacArthur Causeway lanes into Miami's best flat-water kite launch, where instructors and pros share the same sand.
adventure.bonus: Ask a kiter for a quick body-drag lesson and get in the water before you leave.

foodie.title: Fritas at El Rey de las Fritas
foodie.description: The Cuban frita — spiced beef patty, shoestring potatoes, secret sauce on Cuban bread — has a king, and he has held court on Calle Ocho for generations.
foodie.bonus: Frita a caballo — with the fried egg on top — and a mamey shake.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Enriqueta's Sandwich Shop
foodie.description: The pink corner luncheonette on the edge of Wynwood has fed the neighborhood cafecito and pan con bistec since long before the murals arrived — cash, counter, Spanish optional but appreciated.
foodie.bonus: Order the pan con bistec with extra papitas inside — the crunch is structural.

foodie.title: Fried Shrimp Counter at La Camaronera
foodie.description: Standing room only since 1966 — this Flagler fish counter fries shrimp to order and built its legend on the pan con minuta, a whole fried snapper in bread with the tail sticking out.
foodie.bonus: Pan con minuta, tail on, standing at the counter. There is no other correct order.

foodie.title: Late-Night Tacos at Coyo Taco Wynwood
foodie.description: Open until 5 a.m., this Wynwood staple serves tacos al pastor and house-made tortillas to the after-hours crowd without any drop in quality.
foodie.bonus: Show up after midnight and order the taco the person ahead of you ordered.

foodie.title: Pastelitos at Vicky Bakery
foodie.description: Miami's legendary Cuban bakery chain has been cranking out flaky guava-and-cheese pastelitos since 1972 — one bite and the city makes sense.
foodie.bonus: Buy a dozen and hand out the extras to people waiting at the bus stop next door.

foodie.title: Brunch at Mandolin Aegean Bistro
foodie.description: A 1940s bungalow in the Upper East Side with a garden courtyard serves Greek and Turkish mezze that make you forget you're in Miami — almost.
foodie.bonus: Share every dish family-style with strangers at the next table if the terrace is packed.

foodie.title: Omakase at Hiyakawa
foodie.description: A hushed Wynwood counter serving some of the most precise Japanese omakase in South Florida — each course a quiet argument that Miami has grown up.
foodie.bonus: Tell the chef your single favorite flavor profile at the start and see how far it echoes through the meal.

foodie.title: Fresh Catch at Garcia's on the River
foodie.description: This no-frills riverfront fish market turned restaurant has served Miami's freshest catch since 1966 — grilled snapper on the dock while the river traffic slides past.
foodie.bonus: Ask the staff what came off the boat that morning and order that — no menu needed.

foodie.title: Cuban Coffee at Cafetería La Carreta
foodie.description: Order a ventanita cortadito at this Little Havana institution and drink it standing at the window like every abuela in the neighborhood does.
foodie.bonus: Order entirely in Spanish — no English allowed.

foodie.title: Calle Ocho Food Crawl
foodie.description: Walk southwest 8th Street from 12th to 17th Avenue and eat at three windows in a row — croquetas at El Pub, pastelitos at La Rosa Bakery, and a guarapo from any cart.
foodie.bonus: Strike up a conversation with whoever's playing dominoes at Maximo Gomez Park mid-crawl.

foodie.title: Stone Crab Claws at Joe's Stone Crab
foodie.description: Open since 1913, Joe's is the only place to eat stone crab in Miami — the mustard sauce, the hash browns, and the claws are as unchanged as the legend.
foodie.bonus: Skip the reservation line by sitting at the bar and ordering the full stone crab platter solo.

foodie.title: Lunch at Versailles Restaurant
foodie.description: Since 1971 this Little Havana institution has served the loudest, most satisfying Cuban lunch in Florida — the ropa vieja and a cortadito are non-negotiable.
foodie.bonus: Order in Spanish only — use your phone to translate before you walk in.

active.title: Free Yoga on the Tina Hills Lawn
active.description: Bayfront Park's long-running free yoga sessions unroll mats on the Tina Hills lawn with the bay glittering past the sea wall — show up, stretch, leave lighter.
active.bonus: Hold the final savasana until the instructor speaks — no early phone reach.

active.title: Bridge Repeats on the Rickenbacker
active.description: The William Powell Bridge is famously Miami's only hill — every dawn, packs of cyclists and runners grind repeats with the skyline on one side and open bay on the other.
active.bonus: Five summits minimum — sprint the last one.

active.title: Beach Volleyball at Lummus Park
active.description: The courts on the sand at Lummus have run pickup games against the Ocean Drive backdrop for decades — sandy, sweaty, and open to anyone who calls next.
active.bonus: Join a game of strangers and learn everyone's name by the second set.

active.title: Swim the Venetian Pool
active.description: Carved from a coral rock quarry in 1924 and fed by spring water, Coral Gables' municipal pool has waterfalls, grottos, and a loggia straight out of Venice — the most beautiful public swim in America.
active.bonus: Swim into the grotto cave and touch the back wall.

active.title: Skate the Miami Beach Beachwalk
active.description: The paved beachwalk runs the oceanfront from South Pointe toward Mid-Beach — rent skates or bring your board and weave the palm-lined miles like a local with somewhere to be.
active.bonus: Skate the full length of Lincoln Road without stopping at a single shop window.

active.title: Pickup Basketball at Flamingo Park
active.description: South Beach's legendary outdoor courts have hosted serious ballers for decades — show up, call next, and earn your spot.
active.bonus: Hit a game-winning shot, then walk off the court without saying a word.

active.title: Trail Run at Amelia Earhart Park
active.description: Hialeah's sprawling 515-acre park has dirt trails, open fields, and a working farm — a raw counterpoint to Miami's beach scene.
active.bonus: Run the full outer perimeter trail without stopping — that's roughly 3 miles — and feed the farm animals after.

active.title: Stand-Up Paddleboarding at Rickenbacker Causeway
active.description: The calm flat water between the causeway and downtown skyline is the perfect Miami postcard, and you're inside it.
active.bonus: Paddle far enough out to frame the full Miami skyline in one unobstructed view, then take the shot hands-free.

active.title: Morning Swim at Virginia Key Beach Park
active.description: Miami's first Black beach carries serious history and still delivers the clearest, calmest water on the bay side of Key Biscayne.
active.bonus: Wade out to the sandbar and do 10 underwater handstands before anyone else arrives.

active.title: Birdwatching at Shark Valley, Everglades
active.description: Rent a bike inside Everglades National Park and cruise the fifteen-mile loop past roseate spoonbills, anhinga, and alligators close enough to make you pedal faster.
active.bonus: Stop within three feet of a stationary alligator and hold your nerve for thirty seconds.

active.title: Cycling the Old Cutler Trail
active.description: A twelve-mile canopy road through Coral Gables and Palmetto Bay shaded by banyan trees is Miami's best urban ride — flat, fast, and genuinely beautiful.
active.bonus: Ride the full twelve miles without stopping — no traffic light excuses.

active.title: Sunrise Run on the Venetian Causeway
active.description: The Venetian Causeway is a car-lite bridge chain connecting Miami to Miami Beach — running it at dawn gives you water on both sides, herons at your feet, and zero tourists.
active.bonus: Run the full out-and-back (5 miles total) without stopping, then jump in Biscayne Bay from the fishing pier at the midpoint.

social.title: Golden Hour at Sweet Liberty
social.description: The bar that put Miami on the world cocktail map keeps it loose — happy-hour oysters, a neon PURSUE HAPPINESS sign, and bartenders who treat a daiquiri like a thesis.
social.bonus: Order the bartender's choice and guess three ingredients before they tell you.

social.title: Last Call at Mac's Club Deuce
social.description: The oldest bar in Miami Beach — pouring since 1926 — is a neon-lit, cash-friendly dive where models, line cooks, and night-shift cops share the pool table until 5 a.m.
social.bonus: Play a game of pool with whoever has the table — house rules apply.

social.title: Heat Game at Kaseya Center
social.description: The bayfront arena turns Heat games into full Miami theater — 305 energy, celebrity row scanning, and a building that has hung three banners doing it.
social.bonus: Stay through the final buzzer no matter the score — Heat culture forbids leaving early.

social.title: Free Afternoon at ICA Miami, Design District
social.description: The Institute of Contemporary Art anchors the Design District with a serious, always-free collection and sculpture garden — the best zero-dollar art hour in the city.
social.bonus: Ask a gallerist which piece they personally love most — then see if you agree.

social.title: Mojito Crawl Down Calle Ocho
social.description: The stretch of SW 8th Street between 12th and 17th Avenue is the beating heart of Little Havana — hit three bars, one mojito each, no rushing.
social.bonus: Order your mojito in Spanish at every stop — no English allowed.

social.title: Night Out at Kyu Miami Wynwood
social.description: Kyu's wood-fired kitchen and communal energy make this Wynwood restaurant the kind of dinner that turns into a late night without you planning it.
social.bonus: Order something off the menu that you have to ask the waiter to describe — then share it with a stranger at the bar.

social.title: Rooftop Happy Hour at Sugar at EAST Miami
social.description: Brickell's best rooftop bar combines sweeping skyline views, garden-grown cocktails, and a crowd that actually shows up to drink, not just post.
social.bonus: Order the most obscure cocktail on the menu and make someone at the bar guess what's in it.

social.title: Live Music at Lagniappe
social.description: This Edgewater wine garden strings lights over a backyard of mismatched chairs and nightly live music — grab a bottle inside, order a cheese board, and stay until they stack the chairs.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with the couple next to you and get a wine recommendation you've never heard of.

social.title: Sunday Dominos at Máximo Gómez Park (Domino Park)
social.description: Little Havana's open-air domino tables have been slapping tiles since 1976 — pull up a chair, watch the masters, and play a round.
social.bonus: Challenge a local to a game and don't let them see you sweat — even when you're losing badly.

social.title: Jazz Night at Ball & Chain
social.description: A Little Havana bar resurrected from its 1935 original bones hosts live jazz and mambo most nights — the mojitos are cold and the dance floor has no irony.
social.bonus: Ask someone sitting alone to dance — one song minimum.

social.title: Art Walk in Wynwood on Second Saturday
social.description: Wynwood's gallery walk has anchored the neighborhood since the mid-2000s — every second Saturday the studios open late, the street fills, and the murals get a new crowd to witness them.
social.bonus: Walk into every open gallery and talk to an artist or gallerist in each one — no skipping.

social.title: Saturday Night at Club Space
social.description: Space has run marathon raves under its rooftop terrace since 2000 — the real Miami nightlife circuit starts here at 3am when the serious crowd arrives.
social.bonus: Stay until sunrise and watch the rooftop terrace transform from night crowd to morning ravers without leaving.

chill.title: Bayfront Hour at The Barnacle
chill.description: Coconut Grove's oldest house — built 1891 by sailing pioneer Ralph Munroe — sits at the end of a tropical hardwood hammock with a lawn that runs straight into Biscayne Bay. Bring nothing; do nothing.
chill.bonus: Lie on the bay lawn for fifteen unhurried minutes watching the sailboats — phone stays in your pocket.

chill.title: Browse Books & Books, Coral Gables
chill.description: Mitchell Kaplan's flagship has anchored Miami's literary life since 1982 — arcaded courtyard café, author events most nights, and rooms of shelves that reward getting lost.
chill.bonus: Ask a bookseller for one book they would force on a stranger — buy it.

chill.title: Hammock Afternoon at A.D. Barnes Park
chill.description: This underrated 65-acre Westchester park has old-growth trees built for hammocking and a nature center that keeps the vibe genuinely local and quiet.
chill.bonus: Set a timer for 45 minutes and read without checking your phone once — not even to change the music.

chill.title: Sunset Drinks at the Pérez Art Museum Terrace
chill.description: PAMM's bayfront terrace at Museum Park faces downtown and Biscayne Bay — on a clear evening the skyline reflection on the water makes the overpriced cocktail worth every dollar.
chill.bonus: Walk inside and spend five minutes alone with a single piece of art before heading back out.

chill.title: Morning at Crandon Park Beach
chill.description: Key Biscayne's widest stretch of powdered sand is calm, clear, and chronically underrated — the water here actually looks like the Bahamas.
chill.bonus: Walk to the far southern end of the beach where almost nobody goes and stay for 20 minutes.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
chill.description: A Gilded Age villa built in 1916 on Biscayne Bay with ten acres of formal Italian gardens — one of the most quietly stunning places in Florida.
chill.bonus: Find the hidden stone barge breakwater and take a photo that looks like Europe.

chill.title: Dusk at Matheson Hammock Park
chill.description: A man-made atoll pool flushed by Biscayne Bay tides turns gold at sunset while egrets stalk the shallows — Coral Gables' best-kept hour.
chill.bonus: Wade into the atoll pool at exactly the moment the sun hits the water.

chill.title: Quiet Sand at Mid-Beach
chill.description: The stretch of Miami Beach between 23rd and 44th is where the crowds thin, the Art Deco backdrop keeps going, and a towel and a book buy you the afternoon locals keep quiet about.
chill.bonus: Leave your book on the towel of whoever's leaving next to you.

chill.title: Wander the Deering Estate at Cutler
chill.description: A 1920s Mediterranean Revival estate on Biscayne Bay sits inside one of the last old-growth hammocks in Miami-Dade — completely wild ten minutes from the highway.
chill.bonus: Find the burial mound on the trail and sit in silence there for five full minutes.

chill.title: Afternoon on South Pointe Park Pier
chill.description: Watch cruise ships and container vessels pass through Government Cut while pelicans dive-bomb baitfish — Miami's best free show runs on its own schedule.
chill.bonus: Time a photo of yourself against a full cruise ship hull — nail the scale.

chill.title: Sunset at Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
chill.description: The southern tip of Key Biscayne holds Miami's most untouched beach, a lighthouse built in 1825, and a westward view of the city skyline at golden hour that stops everything.
chill.bonus: Climb the Cape Florida Lighthouse and watch the sunset from the top lantern deck.

chill.title: Afternoon at Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
chill.description: This 83-acre Coral Gables garden has been a sanctuary since 1938 — the cycad collection and the rainforest canopy walkway make every visit feel slower, better.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest cycad on the property and sit under it for ten uninterrupted minutes.
